instruction.text: Listen and choose the correct meaning of the word.

b.sound: Sympathy is when you feel sad for someone and want to comfort them.
Sympathy is when you dislike someone and think they are pathetic.
Empathy is when you try to understand how someone else feels.
Empathy is when you appreciate someone very much.

instruction.text: Read the text and decide whether it is an example of sympathy or empathy.

atoms.a: Lyra pets an injured dog as she brings it to the vet.
Henry fell over and is clutching his knee in pain. His mother helps him up and comforts him.
Mr Potter’s wife has cancer. His pupils sent her cards wishing her well.
Matt’s mind goes blank when he sees a maths problem. His teacher is patient and thinks of other pupils who have had the same problem to try to help him.
Oskar recently moved from Sweden to the UK and is unfamiliar with British customs. Michael makes sure to explain them to him when Oskar looks confused.
James requires a wheelchair to move around. His friends always make sure the place they are going is accessible to him.

b: ++When you sympathise with someone, you feel sorry for them.
To show sympathy to someone who is crying, you should tell them they shouldn’t be sad.
++You can show sympathy to someone without understanding exactly what they are going through.
++You can empathise with someone without feeling sorry for them.
++To have empathy for someone means to try to see things from the other person’s point of view.
When you empathise with someone, you should tell them what they’ve done wrong.
